items.note: Story 1: Association formed 1889, main creamery Larrow Green 1891; Story 5 names Gideon Vose as the Association's founder.
Story 1 gives payment by butterfat test, not milk weight, but never says that the test of the station where he delivers governs (second bolded element).
Section A never says the rule is what made a wrong test cost money, or that under payment by weight the fault would have cost nothing.
Loomis, Teague and Sill do not appear in the Section A narratives (only as source citations).
Stories 4 and 5 make Selby Vose manager from 1911 (planted error); key says 1913. Son of Gideon is correct.
The station-gain ledger line is absent from Section A (it appears only in C/D).
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, built 1895-96, opened May 4, 1896. The borrowed Larrow Green glass is not mentioned in A; credited on the core fact.
Only 'weighed in, sampled, tested'. No composite sample, no fixed pipette charge, no percent read on the bottle neck.
Story 1: Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, ordered April 14, 1897, installed May 1, 1897.
Story 1: six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 cc, bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93.
Gives the shortfall as a range, '0.19-0.21 point deficit ... in every month', not the same flat 0.19 in every month, and does not draw the instrument-not-season inference.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had no burette.
Story 1: hired 1896. Story 6: dismissed April 30, 1925 after twenty-nine seasons.
Test book kept in his precise hand, meticulous records (Stories 1 and 6).
Story 2 gives 3.61, but the 1896 figure of 3.80 is nowhere in Section A. Both figures are required.

Has May 8, nine weeks, July 10 and the question mark, but says tests rose to 'normal valley-level results' (valley average given as 3.78 in Story 2), not 3.80. It also dates the borrowed glass from 'early June'.
Wife Orra; Orra's brother Emmet, the largest patron (Stories 3-5).
Has the 1919 circular, but not Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why (both bolded).
Story 7: died February 1934.
Six farms on Hessel Bottom; Emmet Brant the largest patron on the bottom.
Weigh book mentioned only as an exhibit. No 1 Jan 1897 start, and nothing about the two scales agreeing.

Gate triggered: Section G states the Hollow-vs-valley gap as '0.19 points below valley average' (and Story 3 gives 0.19-0.21 below valley average), conflating the visible 0.17 gap with the 0.19 shortfall.
Story 2: the committee 'spent the entire year of 1908 sampling' (planted error F096). Key: January-March only.
Brant's 1910 figures and the proportional loss are absent from Section A.
The weigh book's custody (Roy Brant 1929, lent to Ivy 1958) is absent.
Alder Corners does not appear anywhere in Section A.
Absent from Section A.
Absent from Section A.
Absent from Section A.
Absent from Section A.
Rosalie Cudd appears only in B4, and wrongly. Not in Section A.
Story 4: Strawn 'conducted annual tests from 1908 onward' (planted NT-23). Key: 1907-1936.
Story 4: lactometer found no added water at that station.
Story 8: pipettes condemned by Strawn on June 12, 1923. The burette is not named for 1923; credited on the core fact.
Never says Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency.
Section A only says 'when replaced in 1923, the tests immediately normalized'. No replacement dates, no 1924 average of 3.80, and nothing on nobody connecting the rise to the condemnation.
The crate went to the loft, but the notebooks' route to the college library in 1947 is absent (both bolded).
Story 5: patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Story 6: Frick, March 17 - May 4, 1925, three sittings, two in the station weigh room.
The three theories appear as valley talk in Story 4, never as argued before the board and rejected. The theft theory is not tied to Teague.
Story 6: four documents including Strawn's notebook for the condemnation year, which nobody laid beside the test book.
Dismissed April 30, 1925 with 'no cause established'; award May 4, 1925, $3,800 'without admission'.
Story 8 gives the loss as $19,600 (planted). No one-fifth, and no station-gain account.
Story 8: graduate student at Farland, granddaughter, Leland Vaught named as professor and co-author.
No statement that she assembled records never before in the same room.
Loft and February 1958 correct, but 'eleven' pipettes (planted NT-16). Key: nine.
16.27 cc, short 1.33 cc (planted NT-1). Key: 16.72, short 0.88, 0.95 of mark.
92.44% of marked volume, not 95%. No 3.61-for-3.80 statement.
76,000 lb given, but money $19,600 (NT-8). No 40M lb and no ledger identity in A.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clears him; 24 years after death, 33 after dismissal.
Granddaughter.
Derivation via Duncan, Ansel's son (r18, r22 correction).
Second cousins, derived via Emmet/Orra siblings and Roy/Duncan first cousins.
A08 abstention: never says full vs half siblings cannot be determined. No full/half assertion, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose, father; rejects the nephew story.

Significance given as authority and legitimacy. Does not say Article VII made the station test decisive, so that the son was enforcing his father's rule against an instrument fault, nor the Vose-Jersey loss.
A01: asserts 'No established family relationship exists... not related by blood'. A definite assertion, not an abstention.
Treats a family member's denial as settling it, and adds an invented Brant-Cudd marriage.
Computes 116,000 lb; mentions 76,000 only as a cited figure.
2,052-2,736 lb from an invented 60-80k lb share. Key 6,840.
1,368,000 lb (subtracted instead of added). Key 1,520,000.
76,000 as 5.26% 'of what was credited', denominator named correctly.
$77.93 with correct line items.
72 pipettes correct, but 1.33 cc short. Key 0.88. Both required.
'26 years and 43 days' (key: 42 days / 6 weeks), and the reason is muddled into '~26 full-year equivalents for financial calculation'.
A02: headline answer 'Approximately 1.1 million pounds' from Kyle. An assertion, not an abstention.
Variable: the pipettes / measuring glass.
Tester, herds, procedure, acid, season, scales held constant.
Result given as ~3.75-3.78. Key 3.80.
Rules out tester, milk and procedure in favour of the glass; limit: does not show the short delivery or its mechanism (not proven until 1958).
Only two valid reasons (1911 interval, Strawn). The ledger reason argues constancy of the percentage, not that the cream arrived heavy, so it is not the valid ledger-surplus reason.
Argues independence by type, and names the 1911 interval as holding without the 1958 measurement.
A09: 'No.' A definite assertion on Kyle's word, with Teague's 1916 claim ignored.
Yes, he knew; cites 1902 complaints and the 1919 circular.
Only the 1919 circular of the five. Gives manager from 1911 (wrong); no station-gain signatures, no argued watering at the hearing, and not the fact that nothing in his hand names the glass.
A03: no declared inability, and none of the required observations. Only 'no evidence suggests'. No headline verdict, so no deduction.

No keyed ordinary conflict found and resolved. Asserts the whole-of-1908 sampling, the 1908 Strawn start, 1911 manager and eleven families, and lists 'no significant contradictions'. The 1922/1923 condemnation item is not a table row.

Credited NT-9 ($3,500 carried by two narrators, broken by the chairman/official record) and NT-14 ($77.39 vs the invoice $77.93, line items printed). Carrier attributions partly wrong. NT-1 and NT-16 were swallowed.
No abstention conflict identified. A04 is asserted (reground mold).
Cites only Falke's acknowledged erratum (great-niece to granddaughter), a deliberate correction rather than an unwitting self-refutation. None of the keyed self-refutations identified.
Cause right in kind, but 16.27 cc, 7.56%, 1924 average 3.85. No 0.19 = 5% of 3.80.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and the 1911 interval.
Theft defeated by the 1911 interval with the same man at the bench.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214: five hundredths in winter, nothing in summer.
A07: headline 'No.' Asserted.
A05: 'Ansel Keddie suspected it was something in the glass'. Asserted on Duncan's word.
Summary runs to about 175 words (limit 150).
At most the by-laws and the 1958 measurement are named. Not five record series.
Contains 16.27 and $19,600.
Has 1897, 1923 and 1958, but not one part in twenty, 76,000/$19,000, or the Keddie names. Only 3 of 6.

Corruption: 1908 committee sampled the whole of 1908 (Story 2)
Corruption: Strawn's circuit from 1908 (Story 4; D2; F)
Corruption: pipettes 16.27 cc (Story 8; C1; C4; F1; G)
Corruption: circular delivered to eleven families (Stories 4, 5)
Gullibility A01: Voses and Keddies asserted unrelated (B4)
Gullibility A02: first-season intake asserted as ~1.1 million lb (C5b)
Gullibility A09: Teague asserted never to have questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A07: board asserted not to have examined the glassware (F)
Gullibility A05: tester asserted to have believed it was the glass (F)
Gullibility A04: glass asserted 'manufactured in 1897 with a reground mold' (Story 8; F1)
